t: #3313 Find the Last Marked Nodes in Tree
o: Marking spreads one edge per second, so node i's marking time equals its distance from the root i; the last node marked is simply a farthest node from i (any tie works). Computing BFS from every node is O(n²) — too slow for n = 10^5. Key fact: a farthest node from any vertex is always an endpoint of a diameter. So find diameter endpoints u, v once; for each i the answer is whichever of u, v is farther from i.
k: Last marked node = farthest node from the source (BFS layers = marking rounds).
Any farthest node from an arbitrary vertex lies on a diameter, so two BFS runs give universal candidates u and v.
Answer for i is u or v depending on which distance is larger — three BFS/DFS traversals total.

a.i: Run a BFS from each source and report its farthest node. Directly mirrors the problem definition and is trivially correct, but O(n²) time and memory traffic make it TLE at n = 10^5 — present it only as intuition.
s: For each source i, BFS recording distances.
Output the index with maximum distance.
a.t: O(n²) — n BFS traversals of O(n) each; will TLE for n = 10^5.

a.n: Approach 2: Diameter Endpoints (Rerooting via Two BFS)
a.i: Find one diameter endpoint u by BFS-farthest from node 0, the other endpoint v by BFS-farthest from u. For every node i, a farthest node from i is either u or v, so comparing dist_u[i] and dist_v[i] answers all queries in O(n) after three traversals.
s: BFS from node 0; let u be the farthest node found.
BFS from u; let v be the farthest node; keep dist_u.
For each i output u if dist_u[i] ≥ dist_v[i], otherwise v.
a.t: O(n) — three linear BFS/DFS traversals dominate.
a.sp: O(n) — adjacency lists plus three distance arrays.

w: Always present the diameter approach for large n; the all-BFS version is only for building intuition or tiny inputs. The crucial lemma to justify: the farthest node from any vertex is a diameter endpoint (standard proof by contradiction on path overlaps). Pitfalls: off-by-one in n = len(edges)+1, and forgetting ties allow either endpoint. Follow-up: report the marking time of the last node (just max(du[i], dv[i])), or handle weighted edges.
